title: Home Loan Rate Hike: Higher EMI or Longer Tenure?
description: When home loan interest rates rise, borrowers typically face a choice between increasing their monthly EMI or extending their loan tenure. Increasing your EMI.

faq.q: What is a floating rate home loan?
faq.a: A floating rate home loan has an interest rate that changes periodically based on market benchmarks, such as the RBI's repo rate or the bank's MCLR.

faq.q: How does a rate hike affect my EMI?
faq.a: If you choose to keep your loan tenure constant, a rate hike will increase your monthly EMI because the interest component of your payment goes up.

faq.q: Is it always better to increase EMI than extend tenure?
faq.a: Not always. While increasing EMI saves you interest in the long run, it might strain your current budget. The best choice depends on your income stability, age, and other financial commitments.

faq.q: Can I switch my decision later?
faq.a: Yes, typically you can switch. If you initially extend your tenure, you can usually opt for partial prepayments or increase your EMI later if your financial situation improves.

faq.q: Are there any tax benefits for home loan interest?
faq.a: Yes, under Section 24(b) of the Income Tax Act, you can claim a deduction on the interest paid on your home loan, up to ₹2 lakh for self-occupied property.

faq.q: What is a home loan balance transfer?
faq.a: A home loan balance transfer allows you to move your outstanding home loan from your current lender to a new lender, often to secure a lower interest rate or better terms.
